messages:
Alex: heads-up from this morning's canary: harbor-lite int8 with streaming produced duplicated tool invocations for side-effectful tool 'annotate'. attaching example chunks and a short hypothesis.

Sasha: can you paste the raw chunks? wondering if client or server is at fault. :eyes:

Alex: sure — server emitted a func_call token split across two chunks; client interpreted both halves as separate calls. snippet: 

```
chunk A: {\"type\":\"text\",\"content\":\"...\",\"partial\":true}
chunk B: {\"type\":\"function_call\",\"name\":\"annotate\",\"args\":\"{\\\"text\\\": \\\"test\\\"\" , \"partial\":true}
chunk C: {\"type\":\"function_call\",\"name\":\"annotate\",\"args\":\"{\\\"text\\\": \\\"test\\\"}\n```
client saw two calls.

Jin: interesting — fp16 baseline didn't do this, right?

Alex: correct. fp16 streaming run had no duplicates. int8 seems to change emission boundaries (likely quant decoder flush behavior).

Maria: were retries enabled on the canary? could the client retry a truncated func_call and then the server finish the original?

canary-bot: Canary 1749999988: model=harbor-lite-int8, stream_mode=chunked, streaming_hold=false, retry_policy=client_auto(1)

Jin: that matches: client auto-retry on seeing malformed args + late completed func_call means potential double execution. our tool-layer for 'annotate' is not idempotent, so we saw duplicate artifacts in QA table.

Sasha: short-term mitigations we should deploy: 
- pause streaming canaries for this model variant
- enable streaming_hold=true for int8 canaries to avoid early emits
- add deterministic call_id inside func args and reject duplicates at tool-shim
- client-side buffer heuristic: if func_call args appear incomplete (truncated JSON), wait up to 200-300ms for more chunks instead of immediate retry

Alex: agreed. also want a small benchmark: 500 prompts, compare int8 vs fp16 for func_call_dup_rate and parse_fail_rate. Jin, can you run?

Jin: running small baseline now. script: 
```bash
# pseudo
for i in {1..500}; do
  curl -s -X POST "$API" -d '{"model":"harbor-lite-int8","stream":true,"prompt":"@SAMPLE"}' > out/int8/$i.txt
  curl -s -X POST "$API" -d '{"model":"harbor-lite-fp16","stream":true,"prompt":"@SAMPLE"}' > out/fp16/$i.txt
done
# parse occurrences of function calls per file
```
prelim 100-run numbers: int8 dup_rate=2.8% parse_fail=1.5%  fp16 dup_rate=0.0% parse_fail=0.2%

Maria: those are high enough to pause streaming canaries. Also let's log chunk_emission_id and kernel_seq in telemetry for every streaming emit so we can correlate emission boundaries to quant decoder actions.

Sasha: I'll add a lightweight fuzz harness for chunk splitting to the client lib and a lint rule: if a func_call chunk contains unbalanced brackets or trailing commas, buffer for N ms before retrying. Keep this opt-in for canaries first.

canary-bot: Pausing streaming canaries for model harbor-lite-int8. Owners notified: @Alex, @Jin

Alex: created ticket INF-9521 and assigned to Jin/Sasha/Maria for triage and mitigation work. Long-term fix: runtime should make func_call emission atomic (avoid splitting call marker across emit boundaries) or attach stable call markers at tokenization/kernels so clients can reassemble deterministically. I'll loop in eng-runtime.

Action items:
- Jin: finish 500-run bench, upload CSV + raw chunk dumps (EOD)
- Maria: implement call_id wrapper in annotate shim for canary (tomorrow)
- Sasha: add client buffer heuristic + small fuzz harness (tomorrow)
- Infra/Runtime: investigate emission atomicity and kernel flush scheduling (Alex to ping)

stream-bot: note added: telemetry flag chunk_emission_id and kernel_seq will be emitted in next canary build (flag:stream_chunk_meta=true)

Alex: thanks all. we'll re-enable streaming canaries once dup_rate < 0.5% and parse_fail ~ fp16 baseline.
